column1: Easter Island, or Rapu Nui as it is known locally, is home to several hundred ancient human statues — the moai.
column2: 复活节岛在当地称为拉帕努伊岛，岛上有数百尊古老的人形石像，称作“摩艾”。

column1: After this remote Pacific island was settled by the Polynesians, it remained isolated for centuries.
column2: 波利尼西亚人在这座偏远的太平洋岛屿定居后，小岛在此后的几个世纪里一直与世隔绝。

column1: All the energy and resources that went into the moai — some of which are ten metres tall and weigh over 7,000 kilos — came from the island itself.
column2: 有些摩艾高达十米、重逾七千公斤；造像所耗的全部力量与资源都来自岛上。

column1: Yet when Dutch explorers landed in 1722, they met a Stone Age culture.
column2: 然而，1722年荷兰探险家登陆时，遇到的却是一个处于石器时代的社会。
column5: Stone Age culture|石器时代文化

column1: The moai were carved with stone tools, then transported for many kilometres, without the use of animals or wheels, to massive stone platforms.
column2: 摩艾用石器雕成，随后在没有牲畜和车轮帮助的情况下被搬运许多公里，送到巨大的石台上。
column6: without the use of|没有借助

column1: The identity of the moai builders was in doubt until well into the twentieth century.
column2: 摩艾建造者究竟是谁，直到进入20世纪相当久以后仍有争议。
column6: well into|进入……后相当长时间

column1: Thor Heyerdahl, the Norwegian ethnographer and adventurer, thought the statues had been created by pre-Inca peoples from Peru.
column2: 挪威民族志学者兼探险家托尔·海尔达尔认为，石像由来自秘鲁的前印加时代居民建造。
column6: pre-Inca peoples|前印加时代的各族居民

column1: Bestselling Swiss author Erich von Däniken believed they were built by stranded extraterrestrials.
column2: 瑞士畅销书作家埃里希·冯·丹尼肯则认为，这些石像是滞留岛上的外星人建的。

column1: Modern science — linguistic, archaeological and genetic evidence — has definitively proved the moai builders were Polynesians, but not how they moved their creations.
column2: 语言学、考古学和遗传学的科学证据已确凿证明摩艾的建造者是波利尼西亚人，却还没能说明他们怎样移动这些作品。

column1: Local folklore maintains that the statues walked, while researchers have tended to assume the ancestors dragged the statues somehow, using ropes and logs.
column2: 当地传说坚称石像是自己“走”过去的；研究者通常认为，先民是借助绳索和原木，以某种方式把石像拖过去的。
column5: have tended to assume|往往认为

column1: When the Europeans arrived, Rapa Nui was grassland, with only a few scrawny trees.
column2: 欧洲人抵达时，拉帕努伊岛上是一片草地，只有几棵长势瘦弱的树。

column1: In the 1970s and 1980s, though, researchers found pollen preserved in lake sediments, which proved the island had been covered in lush palm forests for thousands of years.
column2: 不过，在20世纪70和80年代，研究者发现了保存于湖泊沉积物中的花粉，证明岛上曾有数千年一直覆盖着繁茂的棕榈林。
column7: lush palm forests|繁茂的棕榈林
column8: for thousands of years|历时数千年

column1: Only after the Polynesians arrived did those forests disappear.
column2: 直到波利尼西亚人抵达后，那些森林才消失。

column1: US scientist Jared Diamond believes that the Rapanui people — descendants of Polynesian settlers — wrecked their own environment.
column2: 美国科学家贾雷德·戴蒙德认为，波利尼西亚移民的后代拉帕努伊人破坏了自己的环境。

column1: They had unfortunately settled on an extremely fragile island — dry, cool, and too remote to be properly fertilised by windblown volcanic ash.
column2: 他们不幸定居在一座生态极为脆弱的岛上：岛上干燥、凉爽，又十分偏远，无法从风吹来的火山灰中得到充足的肥分。
column7: windblown volcanic ash|随风飘来的火山灰

column1: When the islanders cleared the forests for firewood and farming, the forests didn’t grow back.
column2: 岛民砍掉森林获取柴薪、腾地耕种后，森林再也没有长回来。

column1: As trees became scarce and they could no longer construct wooden canoes for fishing, they ate birds.
column2: 随着树木日渐稀少，岛民无法再造用于捕鱼的木独木舟，于是转而吃鸟。

column1: Soil erosion decreased their crop yields.
column2: 水土流失使作物产量下降。

column1: Before Europeans arrived, the Rapanui had descended into civil war and cannibalism, he maintains.
column2: 戴蒙德认为，在欧洲人到来前，拉帕努伊人已陷入内战，甚至发生了人吃人的现象。

column1: The collapse of their isolated civilisation, Diamond writes, is a ‘worst-case scenario for what may lie ahead of us in our own future’.
column2: 戴蒙德写道，这个孤立文明的崩溃，展现了“我们自身未来可能面临的最坏结局”。
column6: lie ahead of us|在前方等待我们

column1: The moai, he thinks, accelerated the self-destruction.
column2: 在他看来，摩艾加速了这种自我毁灭。

column1: Diamond interprets them as power displays by rival chieftains who, trapped on a remote little island, lacked other ways of asserting their dominance.
column2: 在戴蒙德的解释里，摩艾是彼此竞争的首领展示权力的手段。这些人困在一座偏远小岛上，缺乏别的方式来彰显自己的支配地位。
column7: asserting their dominance|彰显其支配地位

column1: They competed by building ever bigger figures.
column2: 首领们通过建造越来越大的石像来一争高下。

column1: Diamond thinks they laid the moai on wooden sledges, hauled over log rails, but that required both a lot of wood and a lot of people.
column2: 戴蒙德猜想，他们把摩艾放倒在木橇上，让人沿原木铺成的轨道拖行；但这种方法既需要大量木材，也需要大量人手。

column1: To feed the people, even more land had to be cleared.
column2: 为了养活这么多人，还得开垦更多土地。

column1: When the wood was gone and civil war began, the islanders began toppling the moai.
column2: 当木材耗尽、内战爆发，岛民开始推倒摩艾。

column1: By the nineteenth century none were standing.
column2: 到19世纪，已经没有一尊石像仍然站立。
column3: By the nineteenth century|到十九世纪时

column1: Archaeologists Terry Hunt of the University of Hawaii and Carl Lipo of California State University agree that Easter Island lost its lush forests and that it was an ‘ecological catastrophe’ — but they believe the islanders themselves weren’t to blame.
column2: 夏威夷大学的考古学家特里·亨特与加利福尼亚州立大学的卡尔·利波同意，复活节岛失去了繁茂的森林，这是一场“生态灾难”。但他们认为，责任不在岛民自己。

column1: And the moai certainly weren’t.
column2: 摩艾当然也不该为此负责。

column1: Archaeological excavations indicate that the Rapanui went to heroic efforts to protect the resources of their wind-lashed, infertile fields.
column2: 考古发掘显示，拉帕努伊人曾付出非凡的努力，保护那些遭大风吹袭、土地贫瘠的田地里的资源。

column1: They built thousands of circular stone windbreaks and gardened inside them, and used broken volcanic rocks to keep the soil moist.
column2: 他们建了数千个圆形石砌防风围墙，在里面种植作物，还用碎火山石保持土壤湿润。
column7: keep the soil moist|保持土壤湿润

column1: In short, Hunt and Lipo argue, the prehistoric Rapanui were pioneers of sustainable farming.
column2: 简言之，亨特与利波认为，史前的拉帕努伊人是可持续农业的先驱。

column1: Hunt and Lipo contend that moai-building was an activity that helped keep the peace between islanders.
column2: 亨特与利波主张，建造摩艾是一项有助于岛民维系和平的活动。

column1: They also believe that moving the moai required few people and no wood, because they were walked upright.
column2: 他们还认为，搬运石像只需少数人，不用木料，因为人们是让石像保持直立，一步步“走”过去的。

column1: On that issue, Hunt and Lipo say, archaeological evidence backs up Rapanui folklore.
column2: 亨特与利波表示，在这个问题上，考古证据支持拉帕努伊的民间传说。
column3: On that issue|在这个问题上

column1: Recent experiments indicate that as few as 18 people could, with three strong ropes and a bit of practice, easily manoeuvre a 1,000 kg moai replica a few hundred metres.
column2: 近期实验表明，人数少至18人，只用三根结实的绳索，稍加练习，就能轻松地将一尊重1000公斤的摩艾复制品移动几百米。
column5: a bit of practice|稍加练习

column1: The figures’ fat bellies tilted them forward, and a D-shaped base allowed handlers to roll and rock them side to side.
column2: 石像鼓起的腹部使其向前倾，D形底座则方便搬运者让石像左右摇摆、滚动前移。
column7: rock them side to side|让它们左右摇摆

column1: Moreover, Hunt and Lipo are convinced that the settlers were not wholly responsible for the loss of the island’s trees.
column2: 此外，亨特与利波坚信，这些移民并不应对岛上树木的消失承担全部责任。
column6: wholly responsible for|对……负全部责任

column1: Archaeological finds of nuts from the extinct Easter Island palm show tiny grooves, made by the teeth of Polynesian rats.
column2: 考古发现了已经灭绝的复活节岛棕榈的坚果，果上有细小的沟痕，是波利尼西亚鼠的牙齿留下的。

column1: The rats arrived along with the settlers, and in just a few years, Hunt and Lipo calculate, they would have overrun the island.
column2: 这些鼠随移民一同登岛。据亨特与利波估算，只消几年，它们就会遍布全岛。
column4: in just a few years|在短短几年内

column1: They would have prevented the reseeding of the slow-growing palm trees and thereby doomed Rapa Nui’s forest, even without the settlers’ campaign of deforestation.
column2: 它们很可能妨碍了本就生长缓慢的棕榈通过种子繁殖。因此，即便没有移民大举砍伐森林，拉帕努伊岛的森林恐怕也难逃消亡。

column1: No doubt the rats ate birds’ eggs too.
column2: 这些鼠无疑也吃鸟蛋。

column1: Hunt and Lipo also see no evidence that Rapanui civilisation collapsed when the palm forest did.
column2: 亨特与利波也没有发现任何证据表明，拉帕努伊文明随棕榈林的消亡而一道崩溃。

column1: They think its population grew rapidly and then remained more or less stable until the arrival of the Europeans, who introduced deadly diseases to which islanders had no immunity.
column2: 他们认为，岛上人口曾迅速增长，其后大致保持稳定，直至欧洲人到来。欧洲人带来了岛民毫无免疫力的致命疾病。
column4: more or less stable|大致稳定

column1: Then in the nineteenth century slave traders decimated the population, which shrivelled to 111 people by 1877.
column2: 后来到了19世纪，奴隶贩子又使岛上人口锐减，到1877年只剩下111人。

column1: Hunt and Lipo’s vision, therefore, is one of an island populated by peaceful and ingenious moai builders and careful stewards of the land, rather than by reckless destroyers ruining their own environment and society.
column2: 因此，在亨特与利波眼中，那座岛上住着爱好和平、富有才智的摩艾建造者，是精心照料土地的人；他们并非鲁莽行事、毁掉自己环境和社会的破坏者。
column6: stewards of the land|土地的管护者

column1: ‘Rather than a case of abject failure, Rapu Nui is an unlikely story of success’, they claim.
column2: 他们说：“拉帕努伊的故事并不是一败涂地的例子，而是一次出人意料的成功。”
column5: unlikely story of success|出人意料的成功故事

column1: Whichever is the case, there are surely some valuable lessons which the world at large can learn from the story of Rapa Nui.
column2: 不论哪种说法符合实情，整个世界都能从拉帕努伊的故事中学到一些宝贵的教训。
column3: Whichever is the case|无论哪种说法属实
column5: the world at large|整个世界
